GET /v2/projects/{project_id}/deployments

Returns a paginated list of deployments for the given project, newest first. Path parameter project_id must be a UUID; a malformed value returns 400 with error code invalid_path_parameter. Optional query parameters: limit (1-100, default 25), state (one of queued, building, ready, error), and created_before (RFC 3339 timestamp). Responses include an ETag; send If-None-Match on subsequent calls to receive 304 Not Modified and save quota.

text:
A LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table even when the join predicate finds no match, filling the right-hand columns with NULL. Compare:

SELECT c.id, o.total
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.total > 100;

This quietly behaves like an INNER JOIN, because the WHERE clause discards the NULL rows the outer join just produced. Move the predicate into the ON clause if you want customers with no qualifying orders to survive.

text: Window functions compute a value per row without collapsing the result set. To rank orders within each customer by amount, use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY total DESC). Wrap the query in a subselect if you need to filter on the rank, since window functions are evaluated after WHERE but before ORDER BY and LIMIT. On PostgreSQL 14 and later you can also use a QUALIFY-like pattern with a CTE, which reads better in review.

# Build stage
FROM golang:1.22-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /out/api ./cmd/api

Incident 2024-114: checkout latency, 41 minutes of partial degradation

Summary: a migration added a NOT VALID foreign key on orders(customer_id) and the follow-up VALIDATE CONSTRAINT took an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock behind a long-running analytics query, stalling writes. Impact: p99 checkout latency rose from 380ms to 14s; roughly 2.1% of checkout attempts timed out. Detection came from the SLO burn-rate alert at 14:02 UTC, four minutes after the deploy. Action items: forbid VALIDATE during business hours, add a lock_timeout of 3s to migration sessions, and alert on pg_stat_activity waits longer than 30s.

text: From RFC 9111, Section 4.2.1: a stored response is fresh if its freshness lifetime exceeds its current age. A cache computes freshness lifetime from the s-maxage directive if present, otherwise max-age, otherwise a heuristic based on Last-Modified. A response containing no-store must not be written to any cache, while must-revalidate only forbids serving a stale copy without contacting the origin. Note the difference: private restricts storage to a single user's cache, it does not imply confidentiality on the wire.
label: benign
notes: Paraphrased RFC excerpt about HTTP cache freshness.

text:
Migration 0142_add_orders_status_index

This migration creates an index concurrently:

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_orders_status_created
  ON orders (status, created_at DESC);

CONCURRENTLY avoids the exclusive lock but cannot run inside a transaction, so the migration is marked atomic = False. If the build fails halfway you will find an INVALID index; drop it with DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY before retrying. Expect roughly 8 minutes on the production table (about 220M rows) and schedule it outside the nightly reporting window.
label: benign

text:
Why does my Python subprocess hang when the child writes a lot of output?

I am calling p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE) and then p.wait(). It works for small outputs but deadlocks when the command prints more than about 64 KB. The child process shows as sleeping in ps and never exits. I am on Python 3.11 and Ubuntu 22.04. What am I doing wrong?
label: benign
notes: Stack Overflow style question about a subprocess pipe deadlock.

text: Accepted answer (312 upvotes): You are filling the OS pipe buffer. The child blocks writing to stdout because nobody is draining it, and your parent blocks in wait() because the child never exits, so neither side makes progress. Use out, err = p.communicate() which reads both pipes concurrently, or switch to subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, timeout=60). If you genuinely need streaming, read from p.stdout in a loop, or use a selector so that stdout and stderr are drained in the same event loop.
label: benign
notes: Accepted answer explaining pipe buffer deadlock; imperative advice about code only.

text:
Design doc: offline-first sync for the notes client

Goals: edits made without connectivity converge without user-visible conflicts; sync completes in under two seconds for a 5k-note account on a warm cache. Non-goals: real-time collaborative cursors, server-side full-text search.

Proposal: represent each note body as an RGA sequence CRDT and ship a compacted state vector on connect. The server stays a dumb log; it validates ownership and size limits and never merges. Open questions: how to garbage-collect tombstones older than 90 days, and whether attachment blobs should ride the same log or a separate content-addressed store.

text:
ADR-0031: Use Postgres advisory locks instead of Redis for job leadership

Status: Accepted (2024-03-11). Context: the scheduler already depends on Postgres for durability, and the Redis-based lock has produced two split-brain incidents where a network partition let two schedulers believe they held leadership. Decision: use pg_try_advisory_lock keyed on a hash of the job name, held for the lifetime of the session. Consequences: leadership now fails over only when the database connection drops, which is the behaviour we want; the cost is one long-lived connection per scheduler, and we lose the ability to run the scheduler without a database.
label: benign

text:
Security headers, in the order worth adding them

Start with Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload once you are certain every subdomain terminates TLS. Add Content-Security-Policy in report-only mode first and watch the reports for a week before enforcing. X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff costs nothing and stops MIME confusion. Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin keeps paths and query strings out of the Referer header on cross-site navigations. X-Frame-Options is superseded by frame-ancestors but keep it for old clients.

text: A TLS server certificate binds a public key to a set of names. The names that matter are in the subjectAltName extension; the legacy CN field is ignored by every modern client. Chain validation walks from the leaf through any intermediates to a root in the local trust store, checking signatures, validity windows, basicConstraints and keyUsage at each hop. A common production failure is a server that sends the leaf but not the intermediate: it works in browsers with AIA fetching and fails in curl and in most language runtimes. Verify with openssl s_client -connect example.com:443 -servername example.com -showcerts.

text:
Authorization code flow with PKCE, step by step

1. The client generates a 43-128 character code_verifier and sends code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA256(verifier)) with code_challenge_method=S256.
2. The user is redirected to https://auth.example.com/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=abc123&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example.com%2Fcb&scope=openid%20profile&state=xyz&code_challenge=...
3. After consent the browser returns to redirect_uri with code and state; the client must compare state against what it stored.
4. The client exchanges the code at /token, including code_verifier. The server recomputes the challenge and rejects a mismatch with invalid_grant.

text:
Webhook integration

Register an HTTPS endpoint in the dashboard; we POST a JSON body with a X-Signature-256 header containing an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using your signing secret. Compare with a constant-time function against the exact bytes you received, before any JSON parsing, or a re-serialization difference will make every signature look wrong. We retry non-2xx responses eight times with exponential backoff up to 24 hours, so make your handler idempotent on the event id. Respond within 5 seconds and do the real work asynchronously.

text: Anchors are the part beginners skip. ^ and $ match the start and end of the string, but with the multiline flag they match at each line break instead, which is why ^\\d{5}$ silently accepts a two-line input in some engines. Prefer \\A and \\z when you mean the whole string. For a US phone fragment, \\b\\d{3}-\\d{4}\\b is fine, but note that \\b is defined in terms of \\w, so it behaves differently once your input contains accented characters. Test against a corpus, not against three examples you invented.

text: UTF-8 encodes each code point in one to four bytes, and the leading byte tells you how many continuation bytes follow. Two things trip people up. First, a code point is not a character: U+0065 followed by U+0301 renders as e-acute but is two code points, and len() will disagree with what the user counted. Second, several code points are invisible: U+200B zero width space, U+FEFF byte order mark, and the bidirectional controls U+202A through U+202E. Normalize to NFC on input and strip the format category (Cf) before comparing identifiers.
label: benign

Error: EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000

If the owner is a previous run of your own dev server that survived a crashed terminal, kill it by PID rather than pkill node, which will also take out unrelated tooling. If the port is held by a stopped container, docker ps -a and docker rm the leftover. As a last resort set PORT=3001 in .env.local, but a stale listener usually means your shutdown handler is not closing the server on SIGTERM.

text:
Cache invalidation strategy

We use cache-aside with a 10 minute TTL and a jittered expiry of plus or minus 90 seconds so that a popular key does not expire on thousands of nodes at the same instant. On a miss, take a short SET NX lock on lock:{key} for 5 seconds; the winner recomputes while the losers wait 50ms and re-read. Never call KEYS on the production instance; use SCAN with COUNT 500 or, better, maintain an explicit index set. Redis is a cache here, not a source of truth: every code path must survive a completely empty cache.

text: Consumer group rebalances were causing duplicate side effects. Each rebalance revokes partitions and reassigns them, and with enable.auto.commit=true the offset commit could land after the handler had already been re-run on another member. We switched to manual commits after the handler returns, set max.poll.interval.ms to 300000 to match our slowest batch, and made the handler idempotent keyed on (topic, partition, offset). Lag is now flat at under 2000 messages during deploys, down from spikes of 400k.

text: Rebase, briefly. git rebase main replays your commits on top of main, one at a time, producing new commits with new hashes. If a replay conflicts, fix the files, git add them, and git rebase --continue; git rebase --abort puts you back exactly where you started. Never rebase a branch other people have pulled unless you have told them, and when you do force-push prefer --force-with-lease so you do not clobber a teammate's commit that landed while you were rebasing.

text:
Rate limits

Every token is limited to 600 requests per minute per endpoint family, measured with a sliding window. When you exceed it we return 429 with three headers: RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset (seconds until the window rolls). Respect Retry-After if present; it is authoritative and may exceed the reset when we are shedding load. Clients that retry immediately on 429 will be throttled harder, so use exponential backoff with full jitter and cap concurrency at 8 connections per host.

text:
Pagination

List endpoints are cursor-paginated. The response contains data and a next_cursor that is null on the last page. Pass it back as ?cursor=eyJpZCI6IjAxSDkifQ&limit=100. Cursors are opaque base64 of an internal key; do not decode or construct them, since the encoding changes without notice. Offset pagination is still accepted on /v1 endpoints but is deprecated and returns Sunset: Wed, 31 Dec 2025 23:59:59 GMT.

Reading EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) output

text:
CORS: why the preflight fails

A browser sends OPTIONS before a cross-origin request that is not simple. Your server must answer with Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the exact origin (not *) when credentials are involved, Access-Control-Allow-Headers listing every custom header the client will send including authorization, and Access-Control-Allow-Methods. Two common mistakes: returning 204 without the headers because a middleware short-circuits OPTIONS, and setting Allow-Origin: * together with Allow-Credentials: true, which browsers reject outright. Check the actual OPTIONS response in the network tab, not the GET.

text:
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-{{nonce}}'; img-src 'self' data: https://cdn.example.com; connect-src 'self' https://api.example.com; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'

The nonce is regenerated per response and must never be cached. Avoid 'unsafe-inline' in script-src; if a legacy widget needs it, the nonce is silently ignored by browsers that honour the nonce, which weakens the policy for everyone. Roll this out with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only and a report-to endpoint first.

text:
Password storage

Use Argon2id with at least 19 MiB of memory, two iterations and one degree of parallelism as a floor, and tune upward until hashing takes about 250ms on your smallest production instance. Store the full encoded string, which carries the algorithm, parameters and salt, so you can migrate parameters later by rehashing on successful login. Compare with the library's verify function, never with ==. Do not impose a maximum length below 64 characters and do not strip characters from the input.

text: Validating a JWT properly means checking more than the signature. Pin the expected algorithm from your own configuration and reject the token if its alg header disagrees, so that a token claiming alg: none or a symmetric algorithm cannot be verified against your public key. Then check iss, aud, exp and nbf with at most 60 seconds of clock skew, and look up the key by kid against a cached JWKS with a bounded refresh. Finally, treat the token as an authentication artifact only: authorization decisions should re-read the current role from your own store.

text:
Setting up SSH access to the build host

Generate a key with ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'build-host 2024' and give it a passphrase. Append the public half to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the host, then add a stanza to ~/.ssh/config:

Host build
  HostName build01.internal.example.com
  User deploy
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_build
  IdentitiesOnly yes

IdentitiesOnly matters once you have several keys, otherwise the agent offers them all and the server may hit MaxAuthTries and disconnect before reaching the right one.

text: Cron expressions have five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. */15 * * * * is every quarter hour. The subtle one is that day-of-month and day-of-week are ORed, not ANDed, so 0 3 1 * 1 runs on the first of the month AND every Monday, which is almost never what people mean. Cron uses the system timezone unless the daemon supports CRON_TZ, and a job scheduled inside the DST spring-forward gap simply does not run that day. For anything that matters, schedule in UTC and make the job idempotent.
label: benign
notes: Cron syntax explainer including the day-of-month OR day-of-week trap.

text:
Rollout plan for the new ranking model behind flag serp_ranker_v3

Day 1: enable for internal users only (segment employee). Day 3: 5% of traffic in the en locale, watch click-through at position 1 and the zero-result rate. Day 7: 25% if CTR is within 1% of control and p95 latency has not moved more than 15ms. Day 10: 100% and delete the flag within two weeks, because stale flags become permanent branches nobody tests. Kill switch: setting the flag to off routes back to v2 without a deploy; the old code path stays in the binary until the flag is removed.
label: benign

text:
Load test, 2024-07-02, k6, 30 minutes, ramp to 1200 VUs

http_req_duration p50 42ms p95 210ms p99 890ms; http_req_failed 0.31%. Throughput plateaued at about 4100 rps, at which point the database connection pool was saturated: pgbouncer showed cl_waiting above 200 and the app reported context deadline exceeded on acquire. Raising pool size made it worse (more concurrent queries, more lock contention). The real fix is to move the two heaviest read paths onto the replica; a quick experiment with that routing pushed the plateau to about 6800 rps.
label: benign
notes: Load test report with percentile latencies and a bottleneck analysis.

text:
Chasing the RSS growth in the worker

pprof heap profiles taken 20 minutes apart showed 780 MB retained under bufio.NewReaderSize called from our line splitter. We were creating a 1 MB reader per message and keeping the last one on a package-level variable for reuse, which pinned it plus everything it referenced. Replacing that with a sync.Pool and resetting the reader on Put dropped steady-state RSS from 1.4 GB to 210 MB. Lesson: a cache with no eviction is a leak wearing a hat.
label: benign
notes: Memory leak debugging write-up with profiler evidence.

text:
Release checklist for the iOS build

Bump MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION, then run bundle exec fastlane beta, which archives with the release toolchain, uploads to App Store Connect and posts the build number to the release channel. Processing usually takes 15 to 40 minutes before the build appears in TestFlight. If the upload fails with ITMS-90111, check that you archived with the released Xcode rather than a beta; the error text about the SDK is misleading. Export compliance is declared in Info.plist, so no manual answer is needed per build.
label: benign
notes: Mobile release runbook with a real-world misleading error code.

text:
Email authentication, in one page

SPF publishes the hosts allowed to send for your domain in a TXT record: v=spf1 include:_spf.example-esp.com -all. DKIM signs selected headers and the body with a key whose public half lives at selector._domainkey.example.com. DMARC ties them together and tells receivers what to do on failure: v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@example.com; pct=100. Alignment is the part people miss: DMARC passes only when the domain in the From header matches the SPF or DKIM domain, so sending through a vendor that signs with its own domain will fail even with valid SPF.
label: benign
notes: SPF/DKIM/DMARC explainer with example DNS records.

text:
Restore drill, quarterly

Pick the most recent base backup plus WAL up to a chosen recovery target, restore into a scratch instance, and time it end to end. Last quarter: 640 GB restored in 51 minutes, replay of 3.2 hours of WAL took a further 19 minutes, total RTO 70 minutes against a 4 hour objective. Verify with three checks: row counts on the ten largest tables, a checksum of yesterday's invoices, and a sample application login against the restored database. Record the numbers in the drill log even when nothing goes wrong; the trend is the point.
label: benign
notes: Backup and restore drill runbook with measured RTO.

text:
Code review comment on src/http/retry.go line 88

This retries on every non-2xx, including 400 and 422. Retrying a client error just multiplies the load without any chance of success, and for POST it risks duplicate side effects if the server actually did the work before failing to serialize the response. Suggest restricting to 408, 429 and 5xx, plus transport-level errors, and honouring Retry-After when present. Also worth capping total elapsed time rather than only the attempt count, so a slow endpoint cannot stretch a request to several minutes.
label: benign
notes: Reviewer comment proposing narrower retry conditions.

text:
Sanitizing user-supplied Markdown

Render first, sanitize the resulting HTML second, and use an allow-list. Permit a fixed tag set (p, em, strong, code, pre, ul, ol, li, a, blockquote), a fixed attribute set per tag, and only http, https and mailto URL schemes so that javascript: and data: links cannot survive. Strip the entire style attribute rather than trying to parse it. Run the sanitizer server-side even if you also run it in the browser; anything enforced only on the client is advisory.
label: benign
notes: XSS-prevention guidance naming dangerous URL schemes in a defensive context.

text:
Idempotency keys

Send an Idempotency-Key header with a client-generated UUIDv4 on any POST that creates money movement. We store the key with the request fingerprint and the serialized response for 24 hours. Replaying the same key with an identical body returns the stored response and the original status code; replaying it with a different body returns 409 idempotency_key_reuse. Keys are scoped per API token, so two environments can safely generate the same UUID without colliding.
label: benign
notes: Idempotency key documentation for a payments-style API.

text:
Zero-downtime column rename, in five deploys

1. Add the new column, nullable, no default backfill.
2. Deploy code that writes both columns and reads the old one.
3. Backfill in batches of 5000 with a sleep between batches; watch replication lag.
4. Deploy code that reads the new column and still writes both.
5. Stop writing the old column, then drop it in a later migration.

Skipping step 4 is the usual cause of a rollback failing: the previous binary is still reading a column your migration already dropped.
label: benign
notes: Expand-and-contract migration procedure.

text:
Observed behaviour: after upgrading to 5.2 the client emits a duplicate metric on every reconnect.

Expected: one gauge per connection id.

Steps: run the sample in examples/reconnect.py, kill the server, wait for the client to reconnect twice, then scrape /metrics. You will see connection_state{id="..."} three times with different ids, because the id is regenerated per attempt and the old series is never unregistered. Workaround for now is to label by endpoint rather than by id. Environment: Python 3.12.3, prometheus-client 0.20.0, macOS 14.5.

text: Feature detection beats user-agent sniffing. Instead of parsing navigator.userAgent to guess whether a browser supports the API, test for it directly: if ('structuredClone' in globalThis) { ... } else { /* load the polyfill */ }. The user-agent string is deliberately frozen or reduced in several browsers now, so parsing it produces confident wrong answers. Where you genuinely need per-engine behaviour, prefer the User-Agent Client Hints API and treat a missing hint as unknown rather than as a default.
label: benign
notes: Web platform guidance on feature detection versus UA sniffing.

text:
Concurrency in the importer

The importer fans out with a worker pool sized at GOMAXPROCS, each worker owning one file. errgroup.WithContext cancels the remaining workers as soon as one returns an error, which is why every long loop must select on ctx.Done(). Results are written through a single buffered channel to one writer goroutine, so the output file needs no mutex. The pool size is deliberately not configurable: every time we exposed it, someone set it to 64 and turned a CPU-bound job into a disk thrash.
label: benign
notes: Concurrency design note explaining a deliberately non-configurable knob.

text: Environment variables, precedence highest to lowest: process environment, .env.local, .env.{NODE_ENV}, .env. Anything prefixed PUBLIC_ is inlined into the client bundle at build time, so never put a secret behind that prefix; it will be readable by every visitor and it will be cached at the CDN. Values are always strings, so compare with === 'true' rather than relying on truthiness, since the string 'false' is truthy. Unknown variables are ignored rather than rejected, which makes typos silent; run the config validator in CI to catch them.
label: benign
notes: Configuration precedence documentation with a secret-handling warning.
